$doc: Host-authoritative WebRTC P2P. The signalling server (src/server) only brokers 6-digit codes and SDP/ICE; all gameplay traffic is peer-to-peer. See docs/systems/NETWORKING.md.

identity.$doc: A player's name is the only free text in the protocol other than chat, so its cap lives here rather than with the interface that draws it: it is applied to what this player types AND to whatever a peer sends.

simulation.$doc: Host runs the authoritative sim. Clients predict their own movement and reconcile.

connection.$doc: Liveness and the load gate. A browser tab closed without a goodbye never sends one, so peers are dropped on silence rather than on a close event.
connection.$note: Everyone generates the map at their own speed. The host holds the run at the loading screen until every peer reports in, or until this expires - a peer that crashed loading must not strand the rest at a spinner.

hostMigration.$note: Not implemented in v1. If the host drops, the run ends and everyone returns to the main menu.

voice.$doc: Proximity voice over the same peer connections. Attenuation is computed client-side per remote peer.
voice.$note: Attenuation is distance only. Walls and doors do not muffle voice - players are meant to hear each other generously across the map.
voice.$note2: The enemy only gets a noise event above `noiseThresholdDb` - well above the open-mic gate, so a whisper carries to your team and not to the hunter. Speaking re-emits every `noiseIntervalSeconds`; noise events live one tick.
voice.$note3: Speaking indicators: what counts as audible on a received track, and how long the icon lingers so it does not flicker between words.

steam.$doc: Placeholder for the packaged build. Not used in the browser build.
